fatal_errors: The proposed FeCoCrNiMn polycrystalline coating does not match the FeNiCrCoCu FCC coating on single-crystal Cu.
Annealing followed by macroscopic dry sliding replaces the target intervention of temperature-controlled nanoindentation and friction simulation.
The oxide-layer mechanism is unrelated to the target mechanism involving temperature-induced lattice disorder, HCP fraction, and dislocation-density evolution.
Annealing in an inert atmosphere does not by itself establish formation of the claimed stable, coherent oxide layer.
The experiment measures only wear rate and friction and therefore cannot determine whether an oxide layer caused any observed change.
The proposed 700–900 degrees C range and percentage wear reductions are unsupported by cited evidence.
explanation: The response addresses HEA-coating wear in a broad sense, but it does not reconstruct the target material, thermal test series, atomistic conditions, structural mediator, threshold, or outcomes. The target predicts relatively stable hardness through 600 K, sharp softening at and above 900 K, and increasing, strongly fluctuating friction associated with lattice disorder and reduced dislocation line length. The generated hypothesis instead attributes improved wear to an unverified oxide after annealing and predicts reduced friction and wear. Its annealed-versus-as-deposited comparison is testable but strongly confounds oxidation with grain growth, phase changes, residual-stress relaxation, and other annealing effects. Direct oxide characterization and controls for annealing atmosphere would be required even to support this alternative mechanism.
